title: Gulf Med Aviation Services strengthens its fleet with two Airbus H135 helicopters
summary: The acquisition brings the company’s fleet to 12 aircraft and reinforces an operation dedicated to urgent medical missions.
body_markdown:
Gulf Med Aviation Services (GMAS) has acquired two Airbus H135 helicopters, bringing its fleet to 12 aircraft. The two helicopters reinforce the company’s capacity, strengthening its ability to carry out the missions that save lives.


Every mission depends on having an aircraft ready to fly. A strong reserve of helicopters is what allows the operation to keep responding without interruption, including when an aircraft is undergoing scheduled maintenance.


The two H135s expand that reserve, as the activity continues to grow across the company’s markets.


“Our mission is to save lives, and these helicopters are an essential instrument for doing it,” says Simon J. Camilleri, CEO of GMAS. “Reinforcing our fleet is a significant investment in that mission, and in the reliability of the service we provide,” he adds.


Gulf Med Aviation Services Photo


With this acquisition, the GMASfleet is made up of five Airbus[H145](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/airbus/h145) and seven Airbus H135 helicopters, operating across the countries where the company is present. The H135 is a light twin-engine helicopter widely used in emergency medical aviation, valued for its reliability and its suitability for this kind of mission.


GMAS also maintains its own aircraft. This work, carried out under the RotorTechnics brand, covers both line and base maintenance, the routine checks performed between flights and the heavier scheduled work that keeps an aircraft airworthy over time. This capability adds versatility to the operation and supports the readiness of the fleet.


“In this work, being ready is what counts. A stronger fleet gives us a stronger capacity to respond, whenever and wherever we are called,” said Camilleri.


“Maintaining our own aircraft is a real asset for the company. It gives us a close knowledge of each helicopter and more control over keeping the fleet ready for the mission,” concludes the GMAS CEO.


The reinforcement of the fleet reflects the steady growth of GMAS and the demands of operations that, in every country, exist to support those who need urgent medical assistance.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Gulf Med Aviation Services.*
